sections.content: How many people stayed in Bamber Bridge after gaining qualifications?

Bamber Bridge is a medium-sized town in the North West. Bamber Bridge does not have its own university.

Bamber Bridge has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Bamber Bridge ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,265 state-school pupils from Bamber Bridge who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,255 (38%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,175 (36%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Bamber Bridge to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Bamber Bridge's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Bamber Bridge in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Bamber Bridge move to?

Of Bamber Bridge's graduates, 450 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 140 of those graduates (31%) were living fairly locally, in the Preston travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Bamber Bridge's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 355 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 240 of those qualified non-graduates (68%) were living fairly locally, in the Preston travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Bamber Bridge's GCSE cohort:

  • 200 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 70 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 25% of graduates and 25% of qualified non-graduates living in Bamber Bridge had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,050 graduates and 1,050 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Bamber Bridge. This is compared with the 1,255 graduates and 1,175 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 74% of the graduates had also lived in Bamber Bridge as GCSE pupils, while 25% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Bamber Bridge in 2018 to 2019, 75% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 25% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
